'''Holm Gero Hümmler''' (born September 22, 1970) is a German [[nuclear physicist]] and [[skeptic]], living in [[Bad Homburg vor der Höhe|Bad Homburg]], near [[Frankfurt am Main]].

== Biography ==
Hümmler was born in [[Hanau]]. He studied [[physics]]{{r|whoishu|quantenquark-autor|esc-pl|home-science|gwup-whoiswho}} and [[meteorology]]{{r|whoishu|quantenquark-autor|gwup-whoiswho|skepkon}} at [[Goethe University Frankfurt]], together with economy at [[University of Hagen]].{{r|whoishu|quantenquark-autor|gwup-whoiswho}} He was active in politics while at university.{{r|esp}} While working on his diploma thesis he spent several months at [[CERN]] in Geneva, Switzerland.{{r|whoishu|quantenquark-autor|home-science|skepkon}} He completed his PhD at [[Technical University of Munich]] in 2000.{{r|home-science}} He also worked at [[Max Planck Society]], physics department.{{r|whoishu|quantenquark-autor|home-science|skepkon}} Hümmler describes his field of physics as being between nuclear physics and particle physics.{{r|esp}}

He participated in the STAR experiment at the [[Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider]] in [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]], [[Upton, New York]].{{r|whoishu|home-science|skepkon}} He left science in 2001 and first worked for [[Boston Consulting Group]].{{r|quantenquark-autor}} In 2007 he founded Uncertainty Managers Consulting. The company specializes in numerical models for business planning, mainly for the Pharmaceutical and Healthcare sector.{{r|esc-pl}}

He lives and works in [[Bad Homburg vor der Höhe|Bad Homburg]],{{r|homepage}} near [[Frankfurt am Main]].

== Skepticism ==
[[File:Dr. Holm Gero Hümmler.jpg|thumb|left|Holm Gero Hümmler at SkepKon 2017 conference in [[Berlin]]]]
Hümmler has been active in the German skeptics' group [[GWUP]] since 1990s.{{r|whoishu}} He was a regional spokesman and convenor for the Frankfurt area.{{r|esc-pl}} He first became interested in skepticism after reading about the [[European Skeptics Congress]].{{r|esp}} For several years he was an editor of The Skeptiker magazine.{{r|home-skepticism}} He now investigates pseudoscience claims mostly from the areas of pseudo-physics, business esoterics, conspiracy theories,{{r|quantenquark-autor|esc-pl}} supernatural claims in martial arts,{{r|quantenquark-autor|esc-pl|skepkon|home-skepticism}} alleged UFO encounters,{{r|gwup-whoiswho|skepkon|home-skepticism}} weather effects,{{r|gwup-whoiswho|home-skepticism}} biological influence of radiation,{{r|gwup-whoiswho}} misuse of physics terminology in pseudoscience, especially in [[Quantum mechanics|Quantum Theory]] and [[Theory of Relativity]],{{r|home-skepticism}} debunking [[Free energy suppression conspiracy theory|free energy theories]]{{r|home-skepticism}} and [[quantum healing]]{{r|esc-pl}}.

Hümmler appears in media as a GWUP expert commenting on conspiracy theories, such as [[chemtrails]].{{r|esc-pl}} In 2008 he investigated the abilities of [[Shaolin Monastery|Shaolin monks]] on the Galileo Mystery TV show.{{r|esc-pl}}

In a German [[Physik Journal]], an official journal of the [[Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft]], which is the world's largest organization of physicists, Hümmler wrote an article calling physicists to take a stand against the esoteric abuse of science.{{r|physik-journal}}

His first book, ''Relativer Quantenquark'', was published in April 2017. It deals with pseudo-physical claims in esoterics and alternative medicine, but it also explains the basics of quantum mechanics and relativity.{{r|book|gwup-book}} As of July 2017, Hümmler is working on a new book.{{r|esp}}

Hümmler is an author of the science blog ''quantenquark.com''.{{r|esc-pl}} He was a speaker at the [[European Skeptics Congress#17th European Skeptics Congress|17th European Skeptics Congress]] in [[Wrocław]], Poland, where he presented a speech titled ''Relative Quantum Nonsense: Don't be Fooled by False Physics''.{{r|esc-pl}}

== Books ==

* ''Verschwörungsmythen. Wie wir mit verdrehten Fakten für dumm verkauft werden.'' (Hirzel, 2019)  {{ISBN|978-3777627809}}
* with Ulrike Schiesser: ''Fakt und Vorurteil. Kommunikation mit Esoterikern, Fanatikern und Verschwörungsgläubigen.'' Springer Berlin 2021, {{ISBN|978-3662632086}}
